descripcion_geo: Achaemenid Empire with capital in Persepolis and Susa, which dominated the Middle East from 539 BC.
importancia_estrategica: Empire that freed the Jews from the Babylonian exile and financed the reconstruction of the Temple.

historias.titulo: Cyrus the Great decrees the return of the Jews
historias.descripcion: Cyrus the Persian decrees that the Jews can return to Jerusalem and rebuild the Temple; returns the golden utensils.

historias.titulo: Esther and Haman's plot in Persia
historias.descripcion: The young Jewish Esther, Persian queen, thwarts the minister Haman's plot to exterminate the Jews of the Empire.
Nehemiah, cupbearer to King Artaxerxes, obtains permission to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem.

personajes.descripcion: Called 'anointed' by Isaiah; He freed the Jews from the Babylonian exile.
Young Jewish woman who became queen and saved her people from genocide.
Cupbearer to the Persian king who rebuilt the walls of Jerusalem.

contexto_religioso.contexto_lugar: Religiously tolerant empire; his restoration decrees permitted Second Temple Judaism. Setting of the book of Esther and the missions of Ezra and Nehemiah.

judaismo.descripcion: Isaiah calls Cyrus 'my anointed' (mashiach) a century in advance; God uses him to restore Israel (Is 45:1).
judaismo.significado_teologico: Isaiah calls Cyrus 'my anointed' (mashiach) a century in advance; God uses him to restore Israel (Is 45:1).

cristianismo.fuente_primaria: Nuevo Testamento / Padres de la Iglesia
cristianismo.descripcion: The Church Fathers see in Cyrus a type of Christ: the Gentile king who frees God's people.
cristianismo.significado_teologico: The Church Fathers see in Cyrus a type of Christ: the Gentile king who frees God's people.

islam.descripcion: Islam recognizes Cyrus as a possible candidate for the 'Dhul-Qarnayn' of the Quran (Cor 18:83-98).
islam.significado_teologico: Islam recognizes Cyrus as a possible candidate for the 'Dhul-Qarnayn' of the Quran (Cor 18:83-98).
